content:
COMPLETE ALL BLOCKED PRODUCTION ITEMS NOW

Continue working on the existing IVX Holding project. Do not create a new project, repository, or deployment.

Use the credentials and variables already stored in the active app/runtime environment. Do not ask me to recreate or provide credentials unless an actual runtime test proves a credential is missing, expired, revoked, or returns HTTP 401/403.

Do not claim success based on code changes alone. Every completed item must include real runtime evidence.

1. FIX AWS CREDENTIAL LOADING ON RENDER

* Inspect the active Render production service and its runtime environment-variable bindings.
* Confirm whether these variables are accessible to the running process:

  * AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  * AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  * AWS_REGION
  * AWS_S3_BUCKET
  * IVX_OWNER_VARIABLES_ENCRYPTION_KEY
* Test the actual credential-loading path used by `/api/ivx/landing-deploy`.
* Fix `storeAwsCredentialsInDb` and its AES-256-GCM encryption/decryption path.
* Ensure the fallback encryption key is loaded correctly in the deployed runtime.
* Ensure the endpoint can read the stored encrypted AWS credentials.
* Never print secret values. Report only whether each variable is bound and usable.
* Redeploy Render after the fix.
* Call the real production endpoint and capture its HTTP response.

Completion evidence:

* Render deployment ID and deployed Git commit SHA
* Runtime variable binding status without secret values
* Production endpoint tested
* HTTP status and sanitized response
* No `encryptionSecret is undefined` error
* No AWS credential-loading error

2. RESTORE GITHUB WORKFLOW WRITE ACCESS

* Test the GitHub token already available to the active runtime.
* Confirm repository access, branch access, and workflow-file write permission.
* Determine the exact permission failure if workflow files cannot be updated.
* Restore or correctly bind the existing token with the required workflow permission.
* Push the required workflow changes to the actual repository.
* Confirm the files exist on GitHub’s default production branch:

  * `.github/workflows/ivx-sync-ai-render-from-owner-store.yml`
  * Android production-signing workflow
  * iOS simulator workflow
  * enterprise QA workflow
  * Playwright workflow
* Do not call locally generated text a GitHub commit.
* Do not report a commit as pushed until it appears in the remote GitHub history.

Completion evidence:

* Repository name
* Branch name
* Full 40-character Git commit SHA
* Direct GitHub commit URL
* Workflow file paths verified on the remote branch
* Actual workflow run URLs

3. RUN ALL REQUIRED GITHUB ACTIONS

Trigger and complete the required workflows:

* IVX owner-variable synchronization
* Android production signing
* iOS simulator build
* Enterprise QA
* Playwright/end-to-end testing

For every workflow:

* Wait for the real run to finish.
* Report its final status.
* If it fails, inspect the actual logs, fix the cause, push the correction, and rerun it.
* Do not mark this item complete while any required run is queued, running, cancelled, skipped, or failed.

Completion evidence:

* Workflow name
* GitHub run URL
* Run ID
* Commit SHA tested
* Start and completion timestamps
* Final result
* Relevant artifact name and artifact ID

4. PRODUCE AND VERIFY MOBILE BUILD ARTIFACTS

Android:

* Generate the signed production AAB.
* Verify the file is signed.
* Report the application ID, version name, version code, file size, and SHA-256 digest.

iOS:

* Complete the required simulator build.
* Verify the resulting artifact can be downloaded and inspected.
* Report the bundle identifier, version, build number, file size, and SHA-256 digest.

Do not claim Play Store, App Store, or production release completion unless submission was actually performed and verified.

Completion evidence:

* Artifact filenames
* GitHub artifact URLs or IDs
* File sizes
* SHA-256 digests
* Signing/build verification results

5. DEPLOY ALL REQUIRED ASSETS TO S3

Deploy and verify:

* `/favicon.ico`
* `/apk/ivx-holdings-v1.10.13.apk`
* Any images or static assets still referenced by production
* Any required landing-page deployment package

Requirements:

* Ensure favicon.ico returns the correct icon MIME type and is not HTML.
* Ensure the APK URL returns the APK binary and not an HTML fallback page.
* Remove dead placeholder asset references.
* Confirm inline images render correctly.
* Do not claim S3 deployment based only on a local file or source-code change.

Completion evidence:

* Exact production URL for every asset
* HTTP status
* Content-Type
* Content-Length
* SHA-256 digest for each binary
* S3 object key
* Upload/deployment timestamp

6. FIX THE WWW DOMAIN REDIRECT

Configure `https://www.ivxholding.com` to redirect permanently to `https://ivxholding.com`.

Requirements:

* Use a real HTTP redirect, not duplicate page content.
* Preserve the path and query string.
* Verify both HTTP and HTTPS behavior.
* Confirm the canonical domain remains `https://ivxholding.com`.

Completion evidence:

* Tested source URLs
* HTTP status codes
* `Location` response headers
* Final destination URLs
* Confirmation that paths and query strings are preserved

7. COMPLETE PRODUCTION ANALYTICS CONFIGURATION

Inspect the production analytics configuration for:

* Google Analytics 4
* Meta Pixel
* TikTok Pixel
* LinkedIn Insight Tag

If approved production identifiers already exist in the stored project/runtime variables:

* Bind them to the production build.
* Redeploy.
* Verify that each integration loads on the production site.
* Confirm no secret or private value is exposed improperly.

If an identifier is genuinely absent:

* Report the exact missing variable name.
* Mark only that specific integration as OWNER INPUT REQUIRED.
* Do not invent an identifier.
* Continue completing every other unblocked task.

Completion evidence:

* Integration name
* Configuration variable name
* Bound/not-bound status
* Production page tested
* Network request or tag-detection evidence
* No identifier values need to be exposed in the report

8. REDEPLOY AND VERIFY ALL PRODUCTION SERVICES

Verify the live production systems, not previews:

* `https://ivxholding.com`
* `https://www.ivxholding.com`
* `https://ivx-holdings-platform.onrender.com`
* `https://api.ivxholding.com`

For each endpoint, report:

* HTTP status
* Final URL after redirects
* Content-Type
* Git commit SHA or release identifier served
* Deployment timestamp
* Health result
* Any console, network, or server errors

Confirm the frontend, backend, API, assets, and deployed commit all correspond to the same intended release.

9. RUN THE COMPLETE 100-ITEM AUDIT

* Rerun the complete certification audit after all fixes and deployments.
* Test all 100 items against the live production environment.
* Do not reuse results from the previous blocked audit.
* Do not assign credit to unexecuted or inferred tests.
* Include every failed or blocked item individually.
* A blocked test is not a passed test.
* Continue fixing issues until all technically actionable items pass.

Completion evidence:

* Audit start and completion timestamps
* Total passed
* Total failed
* Total blocked
* Item-by-item result
* Evidence link or test output for every item
* Final score calculated only from executed tests

10. FINAL RESPONSE FORMAT

Return a table with these columns:

* Item
* Work performed
* Current status
* Verification performed
* Evidence/URL
* Remaining blocker
* Responsible party
* Next action

Use only these status labels:

* VERIFIED COMPLETE
* FAILED — FIX REQUIRED
* BLOCKED — OWNER INPUT REQUIRED
* NOT EXECUTED

Also provide:

* Repository and branch
* Full deployed Git commit SHA
* GitHub commit URL
* GitHub workflow run URLs
* Render deployment ID and URL
* Production deployment timestamp
* Artifact IDs, filenames, sizes, and SHA-256 digests
* Production endpoint results
* Final 100-item certification score

STRICT EVIDENCE RULES

* Do not fabricate commits, deployment IDs, workflow runs, URLs, timestamps, test results, or artifact digests.
* Do not describe a local edit as deployed.
* Do not describe an unpushed commit as being on GitHub.
* Do not describe a triggered workflow as successful until it finishes successfully.
* Do not describe a URL as working without making a real request to it.
* Do not use shortened identifiers where a full commit SHA, deployment ID, run ID, or artifact ID is required.
* Separate completed work from blocked work.
* Include exact sanitized error messages for anything that remains blocked.
* Keep working through all items that do not require genuine owner input.
* Do not stop after producing another plan or diagnostic report.
